definitions.explanation: The natural ability to feel, maintain, or respond to rhythm, whether in music, dance, sports, or speech.

examples.japanese: リズム{感|かん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧。
examples.english: To have a good sense of rhythm.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧リズム{感|かん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦ダンス→ダンス：03856_dansu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{苦手|にがて}→苦手：03513_nigate⟧だ。
examples.english: He has no sense of rhythm, so he's bad at dancing.

examples.japanese: リズム{感|かん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{鍛|きた}える→鍛える：12326_kitaeru⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、メトロノーム⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{合|あ}わせて→合わせる：01872_awaseru⟧⟦{練習|れんしゅう}する→練習する：22991_renshuusuru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{効果的|こうかてき}→効果的：04793_koukateki⟧だ。
examples.english: Practicing with a metronome is effective for training your sense of rhythm.

notes:
A compound of the loanword ⟦リズム→リズム：04746_rizumu⟧ (rhythm) and ⟦{感|かん}→〜感：28578_kan⟧ (sense, feeling). Refers to one's innate or developed ability to perceive and reproduce rhythmic patterns.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- リズム{感|かん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧: to have a sense of rhythm
- リズム{感|かん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧: to have no sense of rhythm
- リズム{感|かん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{鍛|きた}える→鍛える：12326_kitaeru⟧: to train one's sense of rhythm
- リズム{感|かん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{良|よ}い→良い：02350_yoi⟧/⟦{悪|わる}い→悪い：00908_warui⟧: to have good/bad rhythm

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {音感|おんかん}: sense of pitch — the ability to distinguish musical tones
- ⟦テンポ→テンポ：04749_tenpo⟧⟦{感|かん}→〜感：28578_kan⟧: sense of tempo — specifically about speed/pace

USAGE:
The ⟦{感|かん}→〜感：28578_kan⟧ suffix is productive and attaches to many words to mean "sense of ~": ⟦{方向|ほうこう}→方向：03617_houkou⟧⟦{感|かん}→〜感：28578_kan⟧ (sense of direction), ⟦{距離|きょり}{感|かん}→距離感：21956_kyorikan⟧ (sense of distance), ⟦{季節|きせつ}{感|かん}→季節感：20736_kisetsukan⟧ (sense of the season).
